notes: SHIP v1.14.424 - P0: CUTSHEET ENDPOINTS ARE MASTER DATA. s4:099 RESOLVES ITS 19 REAL COMPONENTS. WHAT WAS WRONG. SITE-HOSTS has been the ONLY source of rack components since v1.6.26, the first Master parser ever shipped. Git proves it: the line that reads column D has been touched by exactly one real commit - the one that wrote it - and the host push is byte-identical today. Cables only ever populated cablesOut and cablesIn. So a cabinet present in CUTSHEET but absent from SITE-HOSTS rendered ZERO COMPONENTS, always. THIS IS NOT A REGRESSION. The capability never existed. v1.6.61 even shipped a host-less cab cabling list around it. In the owner US-SPK03 Master that is not an edge case: SITE-HOSTS carries 4,143 rows and NOT ONE is an s4 cab, while CUTSHEET names 98 s4 racks; 215 of 511 racks (42%) exist only as cable endpoints. For s4:099 the sheet explicitly holds nine GPU-B300 nodes, eight power shelves, an SN2201 and a CDU - with model, DNS and RU - and the phone said NO HOST DATA IN MASTER, 0 COMPONENTS. THE FIX. Every cable endpoint carries LOC:CAB:RU plus DNS plus MODEL. Those are explicit Master records, not inference, so they are normalised into the SAME rack inventory SITE-HOSTS feeds. Build and Forge therefore receive identical data without either choosing a source: both read racksByCab hosts through master_rackToElevation, which derives the U from locCabRu - so components place themselves with no consumer change. THREE RULES, IN ORDER. 1. SITE-HOSTS WINS: if a host already occupies that rack and U, the endpoint is dropped, because the SITE-HOSTS record is richer (serial, role, IPs, grid). 2. DEDUPE BY IDENTITY, NOT BY CABLE: a component is rack plus U plus DNS plus model, so s4:099 68 endpoint references normalise to 19 physical components - one component per cable would have invented 68 devices. 3. PROVENANCE IS KEPT: every component records source SITE_HOSTS or CUTSHEET_ENDPOINT, so a device visible only because something is cabled to it is never presented as though SITE-HOSTS declared it. SOURCE COVERAGE IS REPORTED SEPARATELY (owner ruling): hostsFromSiteHosts and hostsFromCutsheet always sum to the normalised total, so a Master is never summarised as 0 hosts because ONE source lacks ONE cabinet. MEASURED ON THE OWNER FILE, THROUGH THE REAL PARSER: 511 racks, 7,574 normalised components = 4,143 SITE-HOSTS + 3,431 CUTSHEET, 28,264 cables, s4:099 = 19 components at RU46/42/41/40/39/35/32/29/26/23/20/17/14/11/09/08/07/06/02 - matching the owner hand count exactly. s1:002 unchanged at 19 components, all SITE_HOSTS, zero endpoint padding. Compressed payload 1.36 MB against the roughly 5 MB Safari origin quota, so the stress-harness quota cliff is not approached. TESTS: new spec 15-dual-source-master.spec.js, seven tests, all green - and THE DATA IS REAL. Every row is lifted verbatim from the owner workbook (8 SITE-HOSTS rows from s1:001, all 49 CUTSHEET rows touching s4:099, plus 8 overlapping s1:001 cable rows so the suppression path is actually exercised). It builds the workbook in the page and runs the PRODUCTION phantom_parseMaster, not a reimplementation. Pinned: SITE-HOSTS never normalises to 0; s4:099 resolves 19 and not 0 and not 68; the nine GPU nodes land at their explicit RUs; nothing is double-counted and suppression fires; source coverage is reported separately; Build and Forge read one elevation; save and reload preserve components AND provenance. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. No UI surface changed. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: re-import this exact Master and open s4:099 in Forge. It must show nine GPU-B300 nodes, eight power shelves, the SN2201 and the CDU at their stated RUs - not 0 COMPONENTS. Then check an s1/s2/s3 cabinet to confirm nothing regressed, and reload to confirm it persists.
